body.statement: Suppose \(J\ge2\), \(H>0\), \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_{++}^p\), and \(0<\alpha<1/2\).  For the frozen local face space, whose effect vector \(b\) is unrestricted, \(\mathfrak R_{\alpha}^{G}(H,\Omega)=+\infty\).  More precisely, there are two donor-switch faces at any sufficiently small score separation \(c\in(0,H]\) such that every honest confidence kernel has worst-face expected diameter at least \(\Delta[1-2\alpha-v_c]\) for every \(\Delta>0\), where \(v_c=2\Phi(\rho_c/2)-1\), \(\rho_c\to0\) as \(c\downarrow0\), is the total-variation distance between the two Gaussian laws.  Thus the least-favorable two-point sequence escapes through \(\Delta\to\infty\), and the requested finite-valued frontier and finite attaining program do not exist on \(\mathcal H_H\) as defined; a finite formulation must additionally bound the effect spread or otherwise restrict \(b\).
body.proof_tex:
Choose distinct labels \(1,2\in\mathcal J\), which is possible because \(J\geq 2\), and choose a unit vector \(e\in\mathbb R^q\), which is possible because \(q\) is a positive integer.  Fix \(c\in(0,H]\).  Define two score configurations by
\[
h^{(0)}_1=0,\qquad h^{(0)}_j=ce\quad(j\neq 1),
\]
and
\[
h^{(1)}_2=0,\qquad h^{(1)}_j=ce\quad(j\neq 2).
\]
For each \(\Delta>0\), use the same effect vector in both configurations,
\[
b^{(\Delta)}_1=0,\qquad b^{(\Delta)}_2=\Delta,
\qquad b^{(\Delta)}_j=0\quad(j\geq 3).
\]
Each pair \((h^{(\ell)},b^{(\Delta)})\), \(\ell\in\{0,1\}\), belongs to \(\mathcal H_H\).  Indeed, every score norm is either zero or \(c\leq H\), and each configuration has exactly one zero-score label.  Consequently, the implication requiring equal \(b_j\)'s at two zero-score labels is vacuous.  By the definition of \(\tau(h,b)\), the two target values are
\[
\tau(h^{(0)},b^{(\Delta)})=0,
\qquad
\tau(h^{(1)},b^{(\Delta)})=\Delta.
\tag{1}
\]

Let \(m_{\ell,c,\Delta}\in\mathbb R^p\) be the interleaved mean vector of \(Z^{\mathrm{pan}}\) under \((h^{(\ell)},b^{(\Delta)})\), and put
\[
d_c=m_{1,c,\Delta}-m_{0,c,\Delta},
\qquad
\rho_c=\bigl(d_c^{\top}\Omega^{-1}d_c\bigr)^{1/2}.
\tag{2}
\]
Positive definiteness of \(\Omega\) guarantees that \(\Omega^{-1}\) and its positive-definite square root exist.  The effect coordinates cancel in \(d_c\); its first score block is \(ce\), its second score block is \(-ce\), and every other block is zero.  Thus \(d_c=c d_1\), with \(d_1\neq0\), and
\[
\rho_c=c\bigl(d_1^{\top}\Omega^{-1}d_1\bigr)^{1/2}\longrightarrow0
\qquad(c\downarrow0).
\tag{3}
\]
In particular, \(\rho_c\), and hence the distance between the two sampling laws, does not depend on \(\Delta\).

Write \(P_{\ell,c,\Delta}=N(m_{\ell,c,\Delta},\Omega)\).  Because \(\Omega\) is positive definite, both laws have everywhere-positive Lebesgue densities.  To calculate their total-variation distance, transform an observation \(z\) to
\[
x=\Omega^{-1/2}\left(z-\frac{m_{0,c,\Delta}+m_{1,c,\Delta}}{2}\right)
\]
and let \(u=\Omega^{-1/2}d_c/\rho_c\).  Then \(\|u\|_2=1\), the likelihood-ratio region on which the density under state \(1\) is at least that under state \(0\) is \(\{u^{\top}x\geq0\}\), and \(u^{\top}x\) has distribution \(N(-\rho_c/2,1)\) under state \(0\) and \(N(\rho_c/2,1)\) under state \(1\).  Integrating the density difference over that likelihood-ratio region therefore gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\lVert P_{0,c,\Delta}-P_{1,c,\Delta}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}
&=\Pr_{1,c,\Delta}(u^{\top}x\geq0)
  -\Pr_{0,c,\Delta}(u^{\top}x\geq0)\\
&=\Phi(\rho_c/2)-\Phi(-\rho_c/2)
=2\Phi(\rho_c/2)-1
=:v_c.
\end{aligned}
\tag{4}
\]

Now let \(K\) be any measurable confidence kernel satisfying the honesty constraint in the definition of \(\mathfrak R_{\alpha}^{G}(H,\Omega)\).  Let \(Q_{\ell,c,\Delta}\) denote the joint law of \((Z^{\mathrm{pan}},C)\) obtained by first drawing \(Z^{\mathrm{pan}}\) from \(P_{\ell,c,\Delta}\) and then drawing the reported set \(C\) from \(K(Z^{\mathrm{pan}},\cdot)\).  Applying the same Markov kernel cannot increase total variation: for every measurable event \(A\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
|Q_{1,c,\Delta}(A)-Q_{0,c,\Delta}(A)|
&=\left|\int K(z,A_z)\,d(P_{1,c,\Delta}-P_{0,c,\Delta})(z)\right|\\
&\leq \lVert P_{1,c,\Delta}-P_{0,c,\Delta}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}=v_c,
\end{aligned}
\tag{5}
\]
where \(A_z=\{C:(z,C)\in A\}\) and \(0\leq K(z,A_z)\leq1\).  Define
\[
A_0=\{(z,C):0\in C\},
\qquad
A_1=\{(z,C):\Delta\in C\}.
\]
Membership of both parameter points in \(\mathcal H_H\), honesty, and (1) imply
\[
Q_{0,c,\Delta}(A_0)\geq1-\alpha,
\qquad
Q_{1,c,\Delta}(A_1)\geq1-\alpha.
\tag{6}
\]
Equations (5)--(6) and the union bound yield
\[
\begin{aligned}
Q_{0,c,\Delta}(A_0\cap A_1)
&\geq Q_{0,c,\Delta}(A_0)+Q_{0,c,\Delta}(A_1)-1\\
&\geq (1-\alpha)+(1-\alpha-v_c)-1
=1-2\alpha-v_c.
\end{aligned}
\tag{7}
\]
On \(A_0\cap A_1\), the reported set contains both \(0\) and \(\Delta\), so its diameter is at least \(\Delta\).  Hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sup_{(h,b)\in\mathcal H_H}
\mathbb E_{h,b,\Omega}[\operatorname{diam}(K(Z^{\mathrm{pan}}))]
&\geq
\mathbb E_{h^{(0)},b^{(\Delta)},\Omega}[\operatorname{diam}(K(Z^{\mathrm{pan}}))]\\
&\geq \Delta\,Q_{0,c,\Delta}(A_0\cap A_1)\\
&\geq \Delta[1-2\alpha-v_c].
\end{aligned}
\tag{8}
\]
This proves the asserted two-face bound (and it is valid even when the displayed bracket is nonpositive).

Finally, (3), continuity of \(\Phi\), and \(\Phi(0)=1/2\) show that \(v_c\to0\) as \(c\downarrow0\).  Since \(0<\alpha<1/2\) and \(H>0\), there is \(c_0\in(0,H]\) such that \(\gamma_c:=1-2\alpha-v_c>0\) whenever \(0<c\leq c_0\).  Fix any such \(c\).  The effect vector is unrestricted in \(\mathcal H_H\), so (8) holds for every \(\Delta>0\) with the same positive constant \(\gamma_c\).  Letting \(\Delta\to\infty\) shows that the worst-case expected diameter of every honest \(K\) is infinite.  Taking the infimum over all honest kernels in the definition of \(\mathfrak R_{\alpha}^{G}(H,\Omega)\) gives
\[
\mathfrak R_{\alpha}^{G}(H,\Omega)=+\infty.
\]
Thus no honest procedure has finite worst-case expected diameter on the frozen face space, which proves the stated obstruction to a finite-valued or finitely attaining program.
